adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:155 — The test signals completion and asserts without joining the reader, so an in-flight read can fail after the assertion (or never start) and the concurrency regression passes.

adjudication.rationale: The test creates a reader thread that loops while !deletedAll.get(), but after setting deletedAll.set(true), the test immediately asserts on caughtExceptions without joining the thread. This means: 1) The reader thread may still be executing a read operation when the assertion runs, and any exception thrown after the assertion won't be caught. 2) The thread could theoretically never start before deletedAll is set to true, making the test ineffective. This is a real defect in the test logic that could cause the concurrency regression test to pass even when there are actual race condition failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:149 — The reader is neither synchronized to start nor joined, so the test can pass without an overlapping read or before its final request records an exception.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a race condition in the test design. Looking at the diff, the test creates a thread that reads groups in a while loop, then deletes groups in the main thread, and finally checks for exceptions. However: (1) The reader thread is started but there's no synchronization to ensure it begins reading before deletions start, (2) After setting deletedAll.set(true), the main thread immediately checks caughtExceptions without joining the reader thread, so the reader might still be executing its final iteration and could throw an exception that won't be captured. This is a legitimate test design issue - the test may pass even when the race condition it's trying to detect exists, making it an unreliable test.
